content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Philadelphia

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a secondary degree plus documented project-management experience, or a high school diploma with additional experience. Review PMI's education and hours requirements, then gather your employment records and project documentation to verify you meet the credential prerequisites before applying.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Attend synchronous sessions taught by active certified practitioners, participate in real-world case studies, and engage directly with instructors. This formal education fulfills PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and prepares you for exam content.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the bootcamp, create your PMI account and submit your formal PMP application, documenting your project experience and education. Pay the associated exam fee to activate your application and secure your exam eligibility. PMI will review and approve your submission.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to reinforce core concepts. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. Sit for the PMP exam and receive your results, typically within 24 hours of completion.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: Earn professional development units (PDUs) across the three-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. Pursue training, certifications, volunteer service, or authorship that aligns with PMI's continuing-education framework. Renew your credential before it expires to preserve your competitive standing.
